items.title: VZ Keeps Climbing. Should You Climb On?
items.summary: This telecom giant is on a tear, but for investors arriving at the high, the real question is whether the engine has enough fuel left for another lap.

items.title: Verizon Shares Rise 23.3% YTD: How Should You Play the Stock?
items.summary: VZ's cost cuts, customer-focused strategy and AI infrastructure push are fueling gains, but competition and high debt remain key concerns.

items.title: Verizon’s Dividend Is One of the Biggest in the S&P 500—But Is It Safe?
items.summary: Verizon has raised its dividend for 20 straight years and yields nearly twice the S&P 500 average, yet $172 billion in debt and a fresh acquisition are now testing that streak in ways that adjusted earnings alone cannot explain.

items.title: AST Spacemobile Just Moved Its Commercial Launch Target to 2027. Is That Bad News for Its Stock?
items.summary: A disappointing delay sank AST's stock, but it still has a lot of growth potential.

items.title: No ETFs Required: How a 64-Year-Old Built a $5,700 Monthly Paycheck From Five Dividend Stocks
items.summary: Most retirees assume hitting a $68,400 annual income floor demands either a massive nest egg or risky high-yield instruments, but five ordinary dividend stocks across five sectors challenge both assumptions in ways the math makes hard to ignore.

items.title: AT&T Increases 4.7% Year to Date: How to Play the Stock?
items.summary: T gains 4.7% YTD as fiber and wireless growth support momentum, while heavy investment, competition and debt remain key challenges.

items.title: Can Verizon's Disaster Preparedness Boost Customer Satisfaction?
items.summary: VZ prepares network and emergency response resources to help communities stay connected as Tropical Storm Edouard forms.

items.title: Think You Bought a Telecom ETF? You Mostly Own Big Tech
items.summary: XLC carries the word "communication" in its name, but the fund's actual portfolio has almost nothing to do with phone bills, fiber lines, or fat dividend checks. Before you assume you own telecom income, check what you actually hold.
